newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures close lower but losses pared late.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures close lower but losses pared late.

text.p: CME hog futures ended lower but values recovered somewhat late in the session and losses were pared by the close, traders said. Pork bellies finished mixed.
Hog futures closed 0.750 to 0.100 cent per lb lower with April off 0.175 at 74.475 cents.

Early pressure in the hog pit linked to reports of packers closing or cutting back on slaughter operations was tempered by news that one reason for cutbacks was reduced hog supplies, traders said. The supply tightness is bullish to cash hog markets overall and futures acknowledged that by recovering part of the early losses, sources added.

Hog numbers will likely remain tight going into the spring based on trade projections and packers will still be buying hogs. Cash pork prices are also expected to turn higher soon which should boost interest for hogs, they said.

However, pressure was still evident from profit taking. Futures appeared overbought technically and due for some correction to the recent sharp advance that took July and August to new contract highs on Monday, they added.
LFG sold June late while Rand Financials turned a buyer in April after selling early along with Rosenthal Collins, pit sources said.
